source.title: Complexity from Adaptive-Symmetries Breaking: Global Minima in the Statistical Mechanics of Deep Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The supplied paper text is readable. It refers to supplementary material for experimental details, but that material is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains a ReLU VGGNet and reports training risk and accuracy, bearing on whether training reaches near-zero training error. Its binary CIFAR-10, hinge-loss experiment differs from the benchmark recipes in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports one experiment: a 12-layer VGGNet with approximately 10^7 parameters on modified CIFAR-10 for binary classification. It reports loss and accuracy outcomes; details of the experimental setup are referred to supplementary material.
record.test_reason: The study reports zero training hinge loss and training accuracy approaching 1 for a randomly initialized convolutional network on binary CIFAR-10, testing V1 with a modified task and loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under their theoretical assumptions, sufficiently hierarchically large ReLU networks possess pathways to zero surrogate risk. The binary CIFAR-10 VGGNet experiment supplies supportive validation; the authors explicitly require case-by-case study of other sizes, architectures and datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's experiment uses a 12-layer VGGNet, modified CIFAR-10 binary classification, and hinge loss; the cited V1 studies and their recipes are not reproduced here.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper states that generalization to other network sizes, architectures, or datasets should be studied case by case.

fits_no_version.finding: Under assembly-symmetry and diversity assumptions, the authors argue that sufficiently large deep ReLU networks have gradient pathways to zero surrogate risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional symmetry properties of deep-network loss landscapes permit optimization to zero surrogate risk.

record.problems: Only one binary-classification experiment is described in the supplied text; details are deferred to supplementary material. No control condition or uncertainty estimate for the reported training outcomes is given in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Original ten-class CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, comparisons of SGD and Adam, and failures under smaller models, early stopping or regularized recipes.
Two-layer teacher-student problems, spurious-minimum frequencies, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depths and between plain and residual networks; special initialization and Fixup alternatives.
Effects of initialization choices on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate comparisons against a stability threshold, catapult recovery, divergence and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization or Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains the main article and references, but not the referenced supplementary experimental details. Its Hessian analysis does not test V2's specific teacher-student width comparison or V5's learning-rate stability claims. Restricted experimental coverage alone does not warrant limits_scope.
